subject: Renewal & expansion orchestration — timeline, stakeholders, QBR scheduling
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal & expansion orchestration — timeline, stakeholders, QBR scheduling

Anne —

Hope you're well. We're kicking off the PH-4821 renewal + expansion conversation and want to align on timing, stakeholders, and the QBR cadence so we can lock the SOW and updated capacity commitments. Proposed plan below: 

- Week 1 (this week): stakeholder identification & initial usage/health review
- Week 2: SOW draft and internal legal review window
- Week 3: Pricing review & finance approval; DocuSign target
- Week 4: Post-signature onboarding sprint for capacity uplift (prod pass & traffic migration)

Key asks for PolyHealth:
1) Confirm primary stakeholders (procurement, security, infra owner) and their preferred contact info
2) Any constraints on a QBR time window (we can propose 60–90 minute slots)
3) Any required procurement paperwork beyond the SOW?

I'll attach a current usage snapshot and an updated SOW draft for your review — Marissa and Grace will lead the technical/ops side of the QBR. Would Tuesday or Thursday next week work for a 60-minute slot?

Thanks — looking forward to partnering on a smooth uplift.

—
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: SOW_v2.pdf (draft); usage_report_Q1.csv (token breakdown by environment)

Ben —

Thanks for the clear plan. Quick notes from our side:

- Stakeholders: Procurement = Maya Patel (maya.patel@polyhealth.com), Security = Carlos Ruiz (c.ruiz@polyhealth.com), Infra/Platform = Dev Ops Team (platform@polyhealth.com). I'll loop them in after we agree on the SOW baseline.
- Timing: Procurement is tied up the week of the 22nd; best windows are 3/23–3/26 or 4/6–4/9 for sign-off.
- QBR: We prefer afternoon slots (PST) and 90 minutes for the first session to cover usage, expected uplift, and regression monitoring.
- Paperwork: We typically require a vendor questionnaire (security/compliance) and occasionally a shorter addendum for data residency — I'll ask Security to flag anything specific.

Can you share a redline-friendly SOW and a short checklist of what you need from us to accelerate procurement?

Appreciate it — Anne
Anne Keller

anne.keller@polyhealth.com | +1 (212) 555-0127

Anne — great, thanks for the details and the preferred windows. I've attached the SOW_v2.pdf which is intentionally redline-friendly and a short procurement checklist below to share with Maya and Carlos: 

Procurement checklist (what we need to keep the timeline tight):
- Signed SOW + PO or DocuSign completion
- Vendor questionnaire (we can pre-fill common fields) — security team can send specifics to security@redwood.ai
- Billing contact & legal approver name + email

Operational prerequisites for uplift sprint:
- Expected baseline throughput (rps) and target uplift (tokens/min) per environment (prod/staging)
- Whitelisted IPs for private deployment (if applicable) or VPC peering window

Marissa will share the brief usage readout and Grace will spin up a QBR invite with a few afternoon options. We can tentatively target 3/24 2:00–3:30pm PST — please confirm if that works for Procurement.

Ben
—
Ben Carter
